options: How much matter an object is made of
How much space an object takes up
How hot an object is
How fast an object is moving
questions.explanation: Mass is the amount of matter in an object — the real 'stuff', measured in kilograms.
questions.misconception: Volume (space taken up) is measured in liters, weight is gravity's pull — mass is neither of those.

questions.prompt: A 10 kg bowling ball travels to the Moon where gravity is weaker. What is its mass there?
options: Still 10 kg
About 1.7 kg
0 kg
About 60 kg
questions.explanation: Mass is a property of the object itself. Changing gravity or location never changes how much matter an object holds.
questions.misconception: The 1/6 (≈1.7 kg) answer confuses mass with weight, which DOES change on the Moon.

questions.prompt: Which unit is used to measure mass?
options: Kilogram (kg)
Newton (N)
Meter (m)
Second (s)
questions.explanation: Mass is measured in kilograms; newton measures the force we call weight.
questions.misconception: The newton-newton mix-up is the most frequent: newtons are for force, kilograms are for mass.

questions.prompt: How does a balance scale tell you that two objects have equal mass?
options: The beam stays level when both sides hold the same amount of matter
The scale gets louder and louder
The beam tips toward the new object
It measures how fast the object falls
questions.explanation: A balance compares: if both pans are level, the amounts of matter on either side are equal.
questions.misconception: A spring scale measures the pull (weight); a balance measures the equal amount of matter — they answer different questions.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly separates mass and weight?
options: Mass is the matter (kg) and weight is the pull of gravity on it (N)
Mass changes with location, weight stays fixed
Mass is measured on a spring scale, weight on a balance
Both always shrink in space
questions.explanation: Mass measures the matter itself (kg), unchanged by place; weight is the gravitational force on that mass (N), which changes with gravity.
questions.misconception: The swap (mass changing, weight constant) is the classic flip — gravity changes weight but leaves mass untouched.
